technical_and_design_decisions: For U1: Add new 'UNDEPLOYED' enum value to Mesos SPI status model, following existing state machine pattern; update REST API responses and UI components to reflect new status.

For U2: Implement a new REST endpoint (e.g., POST /binders/rabbit/clean) secured with existing authentication; delegate to existing RabbitBindingCleaner service; return appropriate HTTP status and cleanup report.

For U3: Profile YARN deployer to identify bottlenecks; introduce parallel deployment of independent modules; leverage asynchronous operations and caching of YARN resource allocations; ensure backward compatibility with existing deployment descriptors.

For U4, U5, U7: Update dependency versions in build files (Maven/Gradle); resolve transitive dependency conflicts; run full test suite; fix any compilation or runtime issues; update documentation for version changes.

For U6: Modify Kafka binder configuration to allow partition key expression evaluation even when downstream module count is one; ensure native Kafka partitioning is utilized; add configuration property to enable/disable behavior.

For U8: Add a dedicated section in the reference documentation (AsciiDoc) under 'Composed Tasks' detailing HSQL DB limitations (e.g., lack of support for distributed transactions, concurrency issues); link from relevant configuration pages.
assumptions: Developer has full familiarity with the codebase (Spring Cloud Data Flow / Spring XD modules).
Existing unit and integration test coverage is adequate; new tests only needed for new functionality.
Dependency upgrades (SHDP, Spring Integration, Spring Boot, Spring Cloud Build) are minor/patch versions with minimal breaking changes.
YARN deployer optimization has known bottlenecks (e.g., sequential container allocation) and profiling data is available.
RabbitBindingCleaner is fully functional and only lacks REST exposure.
Kafka binder currently suppresses partition key for single downstream module; change is localized to binder configuration logic.
Documentation uses AsciiDoc and is built with existing tooling.
All work is performed by a single developer; no pair programming or extensive coordination overhead.
Integration testing environment (Mesos, YARN, RabbitMQ, Kafka clusters) is available and stable.
Code review is done via pull requests with one other reviewer; effort includes addressing review comments.
